upstream.report: the decode fixture was too small to compress on Go 1.27, so `TestDecodeEvidenceBody` failed on any current toolchain
upstream.outcome: the fixture now has something worth deflating, and the guard asserts the stored-block size ratio instead of a plaintext substring

upstream.report: `ingest_bbot` trusted `scope_distance` from `output.json`, and the allow-list was the only scope gate; a demoted or unscoped item could present as pre-scoped ([#317](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/issues/317))
upstream.outcome: the maintainer chose documentation over a code change: SECURITY.md now states that `scope_distance` is trusted input, that `EvaluateAssetGate` applies block rules whether or not a task allow-list is configured, and that the no-allow-list case is an accepted gap

upstream.report: `record_fact` accepted evidence that never appeared in the intent's recorded work, so a line a target planted could be labelled `tool_output` and still satisfy `prove_goal` ([#124](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/issues/124))
upstream.outcome: the server now ties every fact to a recorded activity or a captured exchange, relabels target-returned bytes as `target_response`, and refuses an untied fact at `prove_goal`; the documented limits are capture-off ties to recorded work, not authorship, and the agent's own output also counting as recorded activity

upstream.report: the `factProvenance` doc comment sat on the struct's closing brace, so it documented nothing
upstream.outcome: the comment now sits on the field it describes

upstream.report: `nato()` mapped A-Z only and silently dropped every digit, so the probe scored text the target was never shown; 56 of 163 shipped payloads carry digits
upstream.outcome: digits now map to the ICAO alphabet (Niner for 9), 186 pass

upstream.report: tool calls cut off by the output cap were still dispatched in the non-chat loops, and the explorer never captured `finish_reason` at all
upstream.outcome: one choke-point guard plus the missing capture, 22/22 CI green

upstream.report: the truncation guard covers the chat path only: the same cut-off tool calls reach five dispatch sites outside it
upstream.outcome: filed with a runtime repro: a scripted truncated round, the real dispatch code, and a real Obsidian vault that gets mutated while history records a fabricated success

upstream.report: provider reported `stopped` while the QEMU process was alive, once the tmp-dir pidfile vanished
upstream.outcome: the fix shipped in 0.8.0: runtime state moved into a project-local run dir, migrated and verified on both of my VMs; what removed the old directory is still unidentified

upstream.report: LXC `mount (rw, move)` denied by AppArmor blocks container start on kernel 7.x

now.title: getmocha.world
now.text: remote job matching that ranks postings before the crowd, then writes your application documents from your own answers: screening questionnaires, CV reads with an honest percentage, cover letters + application emails. Built fail-soft by contract — every AI path has a deterministic fallback, so the product never breaks when the model dies. Kept honest by countables: a real-server jest suite (105 tests across 18 suites), a 62-check HTTP acceptance battery against the live engine, and a browser probe that walks the auth + apply flow on every verify.

now.title: AgentLens
now.text: a harness that scores coding models on first-attempt accuracy instead of final state: fixed tasks in isolated workspaces, a snapshot at every "done" claim, hidden shell checks the agent never sees, and rule-based findings (false done, skipped verification, silenced checks) that point at transcript event numbers instead of opinions. Phase 1 has real local runs through the streamed driver: qwen2.5:7b-instruct and qwen2.5:3b each ran the demo task on 3 independent seeds — 6/6 first-try, 0/6 false dones — and `compare` refuses to rank a model on fewer than 3 distinct seeds. A second phase, inferring done claims from unmarked sessions, is in behind a calibration gate. A hosted Claude run is the next step.
